newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Haggard Australian dlr leans on US$0.7480 support.
newsitem.headline: Haggard Australian dlr leans on US$0.7480 support.

text.p: The Australian dollar was leaning on fragile US$0.7480 support at the midsession after sagging past the imporant US$0.7500/05 bulwark overnight.

Traders said the currency tried to rally after the Reserve Bank again disappointed rate cut speculators, but its struggles were feeble at best in the face of fresh offshore offers around US$0.7495. Pressure on AUD/yen out of Tokyo added to the malaise and dealers expected the market to test the mettle of exporter bids down to US$0.7450 short term.
Data on house building confirmed the recovery underway in that sector, but did nothing to negate talk of another rate cut.
By 12.30 pm (0230 GMT) the local dollar was hard pressed near 16-month lows at US$0.7480/85 having slipped from US$0.7513/18 late here Monday and 76 cents this time last week.
On the crosses the currency down across the board, a fact reflected in the trade weighted index which slid to 56.7 by midday, it lowest level since August last year, from a previous 57.1 close.

It lost ground to a strengthening yen to stand at 84.74/84 from 85.75/85 as the market turned cautious in case Japanese trade date today showed the current account surplus rising to levels which may stoke trade tensions between it and the U.S.
The data are due 2350 GMT tonight, or 9.50 am Wednesday our time, and are expected to show the trade surplus ballooning to around 549 billion yen in May from 229 billion a year earlier.

Today's figures on the domestic econmy fit neatly with expectations of a recovery in the housing sector with dwelling commencements rising 4.6 percent in the March quarter. And starts for the December quarter were revised to a rise of 8.3 percent from an intitally reported 5.9 percent gain.
The trend in starts also turned higher after dropping steadily from a peak in the June quarter of 1994. Analysts saw further gains ahead with housing finance running strong into Q2.
But housing was one of all-too few sectors showing signs of responding to the RBA rate cuts already delivered and did little to shake market conviction the bank would ease again.

Nevertheless, the lack of a move this morning convinced many the bank would not act before its next board meeting on July 1 and 90-day bill futures pulled back seven basis points in response to 94.82. That still implied a rate of 5.18 percent compared to the present 5.50 percent cash rate.
The next real data of importance are May retail trade and building approvals but these are not due until July 2.
